rules: ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.

For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Always resolve account numbers via GET /ledger/account?number=XXXX first, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.
Postings with vatType={"id":0} (exempt) can include both debit and credit lines manually.

Actually 10030 * 0.25 = 2507.50, so it's calculated as 25% of the total.

Wait - in standard Norwegian accounting, "herav MVA 25%" means the VAT is calculated at 25% rate. With 25% rate: gross = net + 25% of net, so net = 10030/1.25 = 8024, VAT = 2006. But the receipt shows 2507.50.

Actually, looking at the field_rules: "VAT type id 3 = 25%". This is from the general mapping. payload.headline: All 5 checks failed: wrong VAT rate (25% vs likely 12%) and incorrect account/structure
what_went_wrong: Used 25% VAT rate (vatType 1) instead of the correct 12% rate for Norwegian train tickets (Togbillett/NSB); the receipt's MVA math (2507.50 on 10030) doesn't match 25% standard calculation.
Manual 3-posting approach with vatType 0 bypassed Tripletex's VAT handling entirely, likely causing VAT treatment check to fail since no proper vatType was assigned to the expense posting.
First voucher POST failed with unbalanced postings error (1 error call), wasting a call and revealing the agent misunderstood how Tripletex auto-generates VAT postings.
Account 7140 (Reisekostnad) may not be the correct expense account for Togbillett; the scoring checks all failed suggesting fundamental account or VAT code mismatch.
what_worked: Department HR was successfully created (id 952435) and associated with the expense posting.
Voucher was created and balanced with correct gross amount of 9600 NOK.
what_to_try_next: Use 12% VAT rate for Norwegian train tickets (Togbillett): net = 9600/1.12 = 8571.43, VAT = 1028.57; use the inngående 12% vatType (likely id 11 or similar) on account 7140.
Try using vatType directly on the debit posting (single posting approach) with the correct 12% input VAT type, letting Tripletex auto-generate the VAT split rather than manual 3-posting approach.
Verify the correct expense account for travel/transport (Togbillett may map to 7160 or 7100 rather than 7140) and confirm legalVatTypes includes the 12% input VAT type before posting.
unnecessary_calls: First POST /ledger/voucher with single posting (vatType 1) that failed — agent should have known balanced postings are required or tested structure first.
Second GET /ledger/account call was redundant since account list was already fetched; could have filtered in the first call.
GET /ledger/vatType call could have been avoided if the correct VAT type IDs were known from field_rules upfront.
